question: What does the term 'act' represent in the context of coding, if it can refer to both a series of acts and a single act?
answer: In this particular code, the word 'act' denotes as well as series of acts as a single act.
llm_answer:
In the context of coding, the term 'act' can refer to both a series of acts and a single act.

The Code (IPC, 1860) makes punishable omissions which have caused, which have been intended to cause or which have been known to be likely to cause certain evil effect in the same manner as it punishes acts provided they were illegal and when the law imposes on a person a duty to act, his illegal omission to act renders him liable to punishment. [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf]

The word 'act' does not mean only any particular, specific, instantaneous act of a person, but denotes, as well, a series of acts. The effect of sections 32 and 33, IPC, 1860 taken together is that the term 'act' comprises one or more 'acts' or one or more illegal omissions.

This is further clarified by section 33 which states that "The word 'act' denotes as well a series of acts as a single act: the word 'omission' denotes as well a series of omissions as a single omission." [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf]

Therefore, in the context of coding, the term 'act' represents one or more acts or one or more illegal omissions.

question: What does the code say about the effects caused partly by act and partly by omission?
answer: Wherever the causing of a certain effect, or an attempt to cause that effect, by an act or by an omission, is an offence, it is to be understood that the causing of that effect partly by an act and partly by an omission is also an offence.
llm_answer:
The Indian Penal Code says that if an effect is caused partly by an act and partly by an omission, it is considered the same offense.

"This Chapter is for the most part an elaborate interpretation clause. It is a key to the interpretation of the whole Code... Wherever the causing of a certain effect, or an attempt to cause that effect, by an act or by an omission, is an offence, it is to be understood that the causing of that effect partly by an act and partly by an omission is the same offence." [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf]

This means that if someone intentionally causes harm or death, for example, partly by not providing food and partly by physical violence, they have committed the same offense. The illustration provided in the code states: "A intentionally causes Z's death, partly by illegally omitting to give Z food, and partly by beating Z. A has committed murder." [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf]

question: What is the punishment for a person guilty of one of several offences?
answer: The offender shall be punished for the offence for which the lowest punishment is provided if the same punishment is not provided for all.
llm_answer:
According to Section 72 of the Indian Penal Code, if a person is guilty of one of several offences specified in the judgment but it is doubtful of which offence they are guilty, they shall be punished for the offence for which the lowest punishment is provided.

In all cases where judgment is given that a person is guilty of one of several offences specified in the judgment, but that it is doubtful of which of these offences he is guilty, the offender shall be punished for the offence for which the lowest punishment is provided if the same punishment is not provided for all. [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf]

This provision aims to prevent an offender whose guilt is fully established from eluding punishment on the ground that the evidence does not enable the tribunal to pronounce with certainty under what penal provision their case falls. The section applies to cases in which the law applicable to a certain set of facts is doubtful, and the doubt must be as to which of the offences the accused has committed, not whether they have committed any offence at all. [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf]

Therefore, if it's unclear which one of several specified offences was committed, the person will receive the punishment for the offence with the lowest penalty.

question: What could be the punishment for a person who gave or threatened for false evidence that led to an innocent person being convicted and sentenced?

question: What does the Code say about a child under seven years of age committing offences and how is it generally interpreted?

In other words, the law does not hold children under seven years old responsible for their actions in terms of criminal liability.

question: What is the punishment for A if he instigates B to murder Z but the offence is not committed?
answer: A is liable to imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and also to a fine.
llm_answer:
If A instigates B to murder Z but the offence is not committed, A will be punished as if B had been capable of committing the offence and had committed it with a different intention or knowledge from that of the abettor.

[A] Whoever abets the commission of an offence shall, if the person abetted does the act with a different intention or knowledge from that of the abettor, be punished with the punishment provided for the offence which would have been committed if the act had been done with the intention or knowledge of the abettor and with no other. [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. 110]

In this case, since the offence was not committed, A will be liable to the same punishment as if B had been capable of committing the offence but did it with a different intention or knowledge from that of A. This means A can be punished for abetting an offence even if the actual crime wasn't committed.

[BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. 110]

However, we must also consider the possibility that B's actions might have been considered as something other than murder, in which case A would not be held responsible for a more severe punishment than what B would have faced. 

[38. Persons concerned in criminal act may be guilty of different offences.—Where several persons are engaged or concerned in the commission of a criminal act, they may be guilty of different offences by means of that act. [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. 38]

Since B was not capable of committing murder (or did it with a different intention/knowledge), A would only be liable for an offence lower than murder.

[BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. 110]

question: What is the punishment for a person who is legally bound to produce or deliver a document or electronic record to a public servant and intentionally omits to do so?
answer: The person shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.

question: What is metal stamped and issued by the authority of the Government of India?
answer: An Indian coin is metal stamped and issued by the authority of the Government of India.
llm_answer:
According to the Indian Penal Code, a metal stamped and issued by the authority of the Government of India is referred to as an "Indian coin".

[BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. 45]

The definition of Indian coin is provided in Chapter XII of the BNS handbook, which states: "Indian coin is metal stamped and issued by the authority of the Government of India in order to be used as money; and metal which has been so stamped and issued shall continue to be Indian coin for the purposes of this Chapter, notwithstanding that it may have ceased to be used as money."

[BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. 45]

This means that an Indian coin is a type of coin that has been officially stamped and issued by the Government of India, and can continue to be considered as such even if it is no longer being used as money.

question: What is the punishment for someone who hides evidence or gives false information about an offence punishable with less than ten years imprisonment?

question: What is 'wrongful loss'?
answer: 'Wrongful loss' is the loss by unlawful means of property to which the person losing it is legally entitled.
llm_answer:

Wrongful loss means the loss by unlawful means of property to which the person losing it is legally entitled.

[BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. 45]

In simpler terms, wrongful loss occurs when someone loses their legally owned property due to an unlawful action or circumstance.

[Comment from BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf]

For example, if a person's bullocks are seized forcibly and illegally in satisfaction of a debt, it is considered a "wrongful loss". [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. 45]

question: What act or omission, if committed in India, would be considered as an 'Offence' according to Indian law?
answer: Any act or omission of which a person is alleged to have been guilty out of India, if he had been guilty of it in India, would have been punishable as an offence.

question: What is considered kidnapping from lawful guardianship?
answer: Taking or enticing any minor under sixteen years of age if a male, or under eighteen years of age if a female, or any person of unsound mind, out of the keeping of the lawful guardian of such minor or person of unsound mind, without the consent of such guardian
llm_answer:
Kidnapping from lawful guardianship refers to the act of taking a minor (under 16 years old if male, under 18 years old if female) or a person of unsound mind out of their lawful guardian's possession without consent.

"BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. 43"] - Whoever takes or entices any minor under sixteen years of age if a male, or under eighteen years of age if a female, or any person of unsound mind, out of the keeping of the lawful guardian of such minor or person of unsound mind, without the consent of such guardian, is said to kidnap such minor or person from lawful guardianship.

This means that even if the accused did not know the person's age or believed they had no guardian, it is still considered kidnapping. The period of detention is immaterial, and it is no defence that the act was not an immediate cause of the person leaving their guardian's place if the accused had earlier solicited or induced them to do so.

[BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. 44] - Anyone dealing with such a person does so at his peril. The circumstance that the act of the accused was not an immediate cause of the girl leaving her father's place is no defence if he had at an earlier stage solicited her or induced her to take this step.

Note: The emphasis on lawful guardianship indicates that this provision aims to protect children and people with mental disabilities from being taken away without consent, even if it was done in good faith.

question: What can happen if a fine, assigned as punishment for an offence that is punishable with both imprisonment and fine, is not paid?
answer: The sentence of imprisonment can be given for non-payment of the fine.
llm_answer:
If a fine, assigned as punishment for an offence that is punishable with both imprisonment and fine, is not paid, the court may sentence the offender to a term of imprisonment in default of payment of fine.

This is according to Section 64 of the Indian Penal Code, which states that "in every case, of an offence punishable with imprisonment as well as fine... it shall be competent to the Court which sentences such offender to direct by the sentence that, in default of payment of the fine, the offender shall suffer imprisonment for a certain term..." [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf]

The term of imprisonment in default of payment of fine is not a substantive sentence but a penalty for non-payment or contempt, and it cannot be added to the substantive sentence so as to see whether the maximum imprisonment that could be awarded for the offence is not being exceeded. [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf]

question: What is the common object of persons composing an 'unlawful assembly'?
answer: The common object of the persons composing an 'unlawful assembly' is to overawe by criminal force, resist the execution of any law, commit any mischief or criminal trespass, take or obtain possession of any property by means of criminal force, or compel any person to do what he is not legally bound to do, or to omit to do what he is legally entitled to do.
llm_answer:
The common object of persons composing an 'unlawful assembly' can be classified into various categories, depending on whether such object is described in section 141 or not. 

According to [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf], "the common object of an unlawful assembly depends ﬁrstly on whether such object can be classiﬁed as one of those described in section 141; secondly, such common object need not be the product of prior concert but may form on spur of the moment, ﬁnally, nature of such common object is a question of fact to be determined by considering the nature of arms, nature of assembly, behaviour of members, etc."

In essence, this means that the common object can vary and may not necessarily have been planned beforehand. The key aspect is whether the assembly's purpose aligns with one or more of the categories specified in section 141.

The five possible objects of an unlawful assembly are:
1. To overawe by criminal force—
(a)the Central or any State Government, or
(b)the Parliament, or
(c)the Legislature of any State, or
(d)any public servant in the exercise of his lawful power.
2.To resist the execution of law or legal process.
3.To commit mischief, criminal trespass, or other offences.
4.By criminal force—
(a)to take or obtain possession of any property, or
(b)to deprive any person of any incorporeal right, or
(c)to enforce any right or supposed right.
5.By criminal force to compel any person—
(a)to do what he is not legally bound to do, or
(b)to omit what he is legally entitled to do.

question: What is the maximum term of imprisonment and potential additional penalties for someone who wrongfully confines another person to extort a confession or force the return of property?
answer: The maximum term of imprisonment is three years, and the person may also be liable to pay a fine.
llm_answer:
The maximum term of imprisonment for someone who wrongfully confines another person to extort a confession or force the return of property is three years.

[Section 348, Indian Penal Code]

"This section provides that whoever wrongfully confines any person for the purpose of extorting from the person confined or any person interested in the person confined any confession or any information which may lead to the detection of an offence, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine."

[BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf]

Additionally, such wrongful confinement can also attract other punishments mentioned in Chapter XVI of the IPC. However, the specific additional penalties would depend on the circumstances and other sections applicable.

Note: The punishment for wrongful confinement under Section 348 is three years, which is different from the two-year maximum imprisonment term mentioned in another section (Section 347) for a related offense of wrongful confinement to extort property or constrain to an illegal act.

question: What is the punishment for causing permanent or partial damage or deformity to, or burns or maims or disfigures or disables, any part or parts of the body of a person or causes grievous hurt by throwing acid?
answer: The punishment is imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years.

question: When does the right of private defence extend to causing harm other than death?
answer: The right of private defence extends to causing harm other than death if the offence being committed or attempted is theft, mischief, or criminal trespass, not of any of the descriptions enumerated in the last preceding section.
llm_answer:

"When a reasonable apprehension of danger to the body continues, the right of private defence of the body extends, under the restrictions mentioned in section 99, to the voluntary causing of any other harm to the assailant. This includes an assault as may reasonably cause the apprehension that grievous hurt will otherwise be the consequence of such assault."

"The right of private defence does not extend to the inflicting of more harm than it is necessary to inflict for the purpose of defence." [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. 125]

question: What is the punishment for attempting to commit offences punishable with imprisonment for life or other imprisonment?
answer: The person shall be punished with imprisonment of any description provided for the offence, for a term which may extend to one-half of the imprisonment for life or, as the case may be, one- half of the longest term of imprisonment provided for that offence, or with such fine as is provided for the offence, or with both.

If the offence attempted is punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, the person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

If the offence attempted is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to one year, and not to ten years, the person shall be punished with imprisonment of the description provided for the offence for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term of imprisonment provided for the offence, or with fine, or with both.

question: If abetment of an offence is considered an offence, does this apply to the abetment of such an abetment as well?
answer: Yes, the abetment of an abetment is also an offence.

This means that if A instigates B to commit a crime, and B commits it as a result of A's instigation, then A can be held liable for the original crime. Similarly, if A instigates B to instigate C to commit a crime, and C eventually commits the crime due to B's instigation, then A is also liable for the original crime.

In this scenario, since abetment of an offence is itself considered an offence, it logically follows that the abetment of such an abetment would be considered an offence as well. Therefore, the answer to your question is yes, the abetment of such an abetment is also an offence.

question: What is the potential penalty for someone who coerces another individual into providing deceptive testimonies?
answer: The individual who coerces another into providing false testimonies may face up to seven years in prison, a fine, or both.
llm_answer:

question: What is meant by the term 'Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty'?
answer: This refers to a husband or his relatives subjecting a woman to cruel treatment.
llm_answer:
The term 'Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty' refers to anyone who, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty.

[BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. 85]

For the purpose of this section, "cruelty" means—any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.

[BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. 85]

This includes the husband or relatives of the husband who engage in such conduct. The term "relative" is defined as a person related by blood, marriage, or adoption and would include father, mother, son, daughter, brother, sister, nephew, niece, grandson, granddaughter, or spouse of any person.

question: What is the definition of 'cruelty' in this context?
answer: In this context, 'cruelty' means any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health of the woman; or harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.

This definition encompasses not only physical but also mental torture or abnormal behavior that can be considered as cruelty or harassment. It is further clarified that "cruelty by itself amounts to an offence" and can vary from person to person depending on the intensity and degree of endurance.

In determining whether cruelty has occurred, relevant factors include the matrimonial relationship between the husband and wife, their cultural and temperamental state of life, state of health, and their interaction in daily life.

question: Who is guilty of abetting an offence according to Section 108A?
answer: A person who, in India, abets the commission of any act outside India that would constitute an offence if committed in India, is guilty of abetting that offence according to Section 108A.
llm_answer:
To whom does Section 108A of the IPC attribute guilt for abetting an offence?

According to Section 108, A person abets an offence, who abets either the commission of an offence, or the commission of an act which would be an offence, if committed by a person capable by law of committing an offence with the same intention or knowledge as that of the abettor.

[BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. unknown]

So, anyone who instigates, conspires, or intentionally aids another to commit an offence can be held guilty of abetting that offence. The person abetted need not be capable of committing an offence, nor have any guilty intention or knowledge.

[BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. unknown]

Therefore, the correct answer is: **anyone who instigates, conspires, or intentionally aids another to commit an offence**.

[BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. unknown]

question: What is the minimum punishment for trafficking?
answer: The minimum punishment for trafficking is rigorous imprisonment for a term not less than seven years, and a fine.

The minimum punishment for trafficking is rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years, but which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

This can be seen from Section 370(2) of the context, which states: "[W]hoever commits the offence of trafficking shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years, but which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine."

The punishment can vary depending on the circumstances, such as the involvement of more than one person or minor, which can increase the minimum punishment to ten years or even life imprisonment. However, in the most basic scenario, the minimum sentence is seven years.

question: Can the appropriate Government commute the punishment for any other punishment provided by this Code without the consent of the offender, if the sentence of death has been passed?
answer: Yes, in cases where the sentence of death has been passed, the appropriate Government may commute the punishment for any other punishment provided by this Code without the consent of the offender.
llm_answer:
The appropriate Government can commute the punishment for any other punishment provided by this Code without the consent of the offender, if the sentence of death has been passed.

This is as per section 54 of the Indian Penal Code, which states that "[t]he appropriate Government may, without the consent of the offender, commute the punishment for any other punishment provided by this Code." [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf]

In other words, the Government has the power to commute a death sentence to a less severe punishment without consulting the offender. This is an important aspect of the Indian penal system, allowing for flexibility and mercy in sentencing decisions. [Indian Penal Code Book.pdf]

question: What is described in section 333 regarding harm to a public servant?
answer: Section 333 describes 'voluntarily causing grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty', which refers to the act of intentionally causing serious physical harm to a public servant with the aim of preventing them from performing their duties.

According to Section 333 of the IPC, whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt to any person being a public servant in the discharge of his duty as such public servant, or with intent to prevent or deter that person or any other public servant from discharging his duty as such public servant, shall be punished.

This section specifically deals with causing grievous hurt to a public servant for deterring them from their duties. The punishment mentioned is imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and the offender shall also be liable to fine. [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, chunk provided]

For instance, if someone voluntarily causes serious harm to a police officer who is performing his duty, or attempts to prevent him from doing so, they can be charged under this section. This law aims to protect public servants from physical harm while they are carrying out their duties. [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, chunk provided]

question: What action would be considered an offence as per section 153B, involving members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community?
answer: Making or publishing any imputation that they cannot bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution is considered an offence under section 153B.
llm_answer:
The action that would be considered an offence as per section 153B, involving members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, is:

**Imputing disaffection or creating enmity**

"...makes or publishes any imputation that any class of persons cannot, by reason of their being members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India..."

or

"...makes or publishes any assertion, counsel, plea or appeal concerning the obligation of any class of persons, by reason of their being members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, and such assertion, counsel, plea or appeal causes or is likely to cause disharmony or feelings of enmity or hatred or ill-will between such members and other persons..."

[BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. 45]

This section provides for punishment with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. If the offence is committed in any place of worship or in any assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, the punishment can be up to five years and also liable to fine.

question: What does a situation where a marriage ceremony is deceitfully conducted without a legal marriage taking place refer to?
answer: It refers to 'Marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage'.
llm_answer:
A situation where a marriage ceremony is deceitfully conducted without a legal marriage taking place refers to [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, chunk 12] "Whoever, dishonestly or with a fraudulent intention, goes through the ceremony of being married, knowing that he is not thereby lawfully married, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine."

This is explicitly stated in section 496 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), which deals with "Marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage." [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, chunk 12] The key elements of this offense are a dishonest or fraudulent intention to go through the marriage ceremony, knowing that it does not constitute a lawful marriage.

The section requires two essentials: (1) Dishonestly or with a fraudulent intention going through the ceremony of marriage, and (2) Knowledge on the part of the person going through the ceremony that he is not thereby lawfully married. [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, chunk 12] These conditions are essential for determining whether this offense has been committed.

Therefore, if a marriage ceremony is deceitfully conducted without a legal marriage taking place, the perpetrator can be charged under section 496 of the IPC, as stated in the relevant BNS chunks.

question: What happens if someone fraudulently causes an order to be executed against him after it has been satisfied?
answer: The person can be punished with imprisonment of up to two years, or with a fine, or with both.
llm_answer:
If someone fraudulently causes an order to be executed against him after it has been satisfied, they can be held liable for forgery.

[BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. 45] "B, though he executes the lease in his own name, commits forgery by antedating it." This suggests that if someone fraudulently causes an order to be executed against them after it has been satisfied, they can be considered to have committed forgery.

This is further supported by [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, p. 46] "Where the accused, after the execution and registration of a document, which was not required by law to be attested, added his name to the document as an attesting witness, it was held that his act was neither fraudulent nor dishonest and the accused was, therefore, not guilty of forgery." However, in this case, the person is adding their name after the fact, whereas if someone fraudulently causes an order to be executed against them after it has been satisfied, it implies a more active attempt to deceive.

The key phrase here is "fraudulently causes" which suggests that the person has intentionally tried to deceive others into believing that the order had not been satisfied. Therefore, if someone does this, they can indeed be held liable for forgery under Indian law.

question: What is the punishment for a person who disobeys quarantine rules?

However, if such disobedience causes or tends to cause danger to human life, health, or safety, the punishment could be more severe.

answer: The maximum sentence is imprisonment for life, to which fine may be added, or imprisonment which may extend to three years, to which fine may be added, or with fine.
llm_answer:
The maximum sentence, including potential fines, that can be given for crimes of disaffection towards the Government established by law in India is imprisonment for life, to which fine may be added.

According to Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, chunk 12], "Whoever by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representation, or otherwise, brings or attempts to bring into hatred or contempt, or excites or attempts to excite disaffection towards, the Government established by law in India, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, to which fine may be added, or with imprisonment which may extend to three years, to which fine may be added, or with fine."

This section further clarifies that "disaffection" includes disloyalty and all feelings of enmity [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, chunk 12]. However, comments expressing disapprobation of the measures of the Government with a view to obtain their alteration by lawful means, without exciting or attempting to excite hatred, contempt or disaffection, do not constitute an offence under this section [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf, chunk 12].

Therefore, the maximum sentence for crimes of disaffection towards the Government established by law in India is imprisonment for life, to which fine may be added.

question: What happens to a person who was sentenced and given remission of punishment but violates the conditions of that remission?
answer: The person receives the punishment to which they were originally sentenced, if they have already suffered no part of that punishment. If they have suffered any part of that punishment, then they receive so much of that punishment as they have not already suffered.
llm_answer:
If a person who was sentenced and given remission of punishment but violates the conditions of that remission, they will be punished with the same consequences as contemplated under section 432(3) [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf].

According to section 227 of the IPC, "Whoever, having accepted any conditional remission of punishment, knowingly violates any condition on which such remission was granted, shall be punished with the punishment to which he was originally sentenced..." [Indian Penal Code Book.pdf, chunk 12]. If they have already suffered no part of that punishment, they will be punished with the original sentence. However, if they have suffered any part of that punishment, then they will be punished with imprisonment or by a term in excess of 14 years, and further directed not to be released from prison for the rest of their life or for the actual term as specified in the order [BNS Delhi police 2nd edition.pdf].

This means that if someone has accepted remission of punishment on certain conditions and then violates those conditions, they can face severe consequences, including being imprisoned again or having their release delayed. The exact punishment will depend on whether they have already served any part of their original sentence [Indian Penal Code Book.pdf, chunk 12].
